_note: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES reference for the StewardMD onco-iotox engine (Phase 8 P2). This is NOT a dosing table. It carries only the general, grade-based management PRINCIPLE for each organ system (continue vs withhold vs permanently discontinue the checkpoint inhibitor; whether corticosteroids are indicated; when to escalate to second-line immunosuppression), grounded in the published ASCO, NCCN and SITC irAE guidance and cited by NAME only. Specific corticosteroid doses, tapers, time windows, second-line agent choices and laboratory thresholds are DELIBERATELY omitted and marked as a gap; they must be read from the current guideline and institutional protocol. Every organ entry is flagged requiresR1Verification. Do not add a drug dose, a mg/kg value, a taper duration or a numeric threshold to this file: the engine's fabrication audit fails closed on any such specific.
gapMessage: Specific corticosteroid doses, tapers, time windows, second-line agents and lab thresholds are intentionally not reproduced here. Consult the current ASCO, NCCN or SITC irAE guideline and your institutional protocol.
generalPrinciples: Grade the irAE and manage by grade and organ, per ASCO / NCCN / SITC guidance.
Grade 1 (most organs): generally continue the checkpoint inhibitor with close monitoring and supportive care.
Grade 2: generally withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; corticosteroids are often indicated; resume when the toxicity has improved toward baseline.

Grade 3: withhold or, for some organs, permanently discontinue; systemic corticosteroids are indicated; if there is no improvement within the guideline-specified window, add second-line immunosuppression.
Grade 4: permanently discontinue the checkpoint inhibitor for most organ toxicities; hospitalize; high-intensity systemic corticosteroids and early second-line immunosuppression per guideline.
Endocrinopathies are an exception: many are managed with hormone replacement and the checkpoint inhibitor is often continued, rather than with immunosuppression.
Exact doses, tapers, escalation time windows and second-line agent choices are guideline- and organ-specific and are not reproduced here.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; topical supportive care and monitoring.
grades.2: Continue or withhold per guideline; topical corticosteroids and symptom control; consider systemic corticosteroids if persistent.
grades.3: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; systemic corticosteroids; dermatology input; escalate if no improvement.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize; systemic corticosteroids; urgent dermatology input and consideration of second-line immunosuppression for severe or bullous reactions.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor with close monitoring; supportive care and hydration.
grades.2: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; systemic corticosteroids are usually indicated; exclude infection; consider endoscopy per guideline.
grades.3: Withhold or permanently discontinue per guideline; systemic corticosteroids; if refractory within the guideline window, add a second-line immunosuppressant.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize; systemic corticosteroids and early second-line immunosuppression for steroid-refractory disease.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; monitor liver function tests more frequently.
grades.2: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; exclude other causes; consider corticosteroids if it persists or worsens.
grades.3: Withhold or permanently discontinue per guideline; systemic corticosteroids; if no improvement within the guideline window, add second-line immunosuppression.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize; systemic corticosteroids and second-line immunosuppression for steroid-refractory hepatitis; hepatology input.

grades.1: Consider withholding and monitor closely; re-image per guideline; exclude infection.
grades.2: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; systemic corticosteroids; exclude infection; pulmonology input.
grades.3: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize; systemic corticosteroids; if no improvement within the guideline window, add second-line immunosuppression.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize (possible ICU); high-intensity corticosteroids and early second-line immunosuppression; respiratory support as needed.

organs.organ: Endocrine (thyroid, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency, type 1 diabetes)

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; monitor the relevant endocrine axis.
grades.2: Often continue with hormone replacement (thyroid, adrenal, pituitary) rather than immunosuppression; endocrinology input.
grades.3: Withhold until acute symptoms are controlled; hormone replacement; corticosteroids mainly for acute hypophysitis or adrenal crisis (mass effect / stress cover), not routinely for the endocrinopathy itself.
grades.4: Withhold and stabilize (e.g. adrenal crisis, diabetic ketoacidosis); hormone replacement and acute inpatient management; endocrinology input.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; begin physiologic hydrocortisone replacement and monitor; endocrinology input. Do not use immunosuppressive corticosteroids to suppress the endocrinopathy itself.
grades.2: Often continue with hydrocortisone (and fludrocortisone if needed) replacement rather than immunosuppression; endocrinology input; educate on sick-day stress dosing.
grades.3: Withhold until acute symptoms are controlled; stress-dose hydrocortisone and supportive care; endocrinology input; resume once replaced and stable.
grades.4: Withhold and hospitalize; treat adrenal crisis with intravenous stress-dose hydrocortisone and fluids; endocrinology input; resume once replaced and stable.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; hormone replacement as indicated (hydrocortisone first, then levothyroxine if needed); monitor pituitary axes; endocrinology input.
grades.2: Often continue with hormone replacement rather than immunosuppression; MRI of the pituitary; endocrinology input; higher-dose corticosteroids only for mass effect, severe headache or visual changes.
grades.3: Withhold until acute symptoms are controlled; hormone replacement; higher-dose corticosteroids for severe headache, visual changes or mass effect; endocrinology input.
grades.4: Withhold and hospitalize; hormone replacement and acute stabilization; higher-dose corticosteroids for mass effect or visual compromise; urgent endocrinology and ophthalmology or neurosurgical input as needed.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; monitor TSH; begin levothyroxine replacement if symptomatic. Corticosteroids are not indicated.
grades.2: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor with levothyroxine replacement; monitor TSH and titrate; endocrinology input if needed. Corticosteroids are not indicated.
grades.3: Withhold until symptoms are controlled; levothyroxine replacement; endocrinology input; resume once stable. Corticosteroids are not indicated for the endocrinopathy.
grades.4: Withhold and hospitalize for severe presentation (e.g. myxedema); levothyroxine replacement and supportive care; endocrinology input; resume once stable.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; monitor thyroid function; beta-blocker for symptoms. Thyrotoxicosis is usually transient and may progress to hypothyroidism.
grades.2: Continue or withhold per guideline; beta-blocker for symptomatic thyrotoxicosis; monitor for progression to hypothyroidism; endocrinology input. Corticosteroids are rarely needed.
grades.3: Withhold until symptoms are controlled; beta-blocker; corticosteroids only for severe thyroiditis; endocrinology input; monitor for progression to hypothyroidism.
grades.4: Withhold and hospitalize (e.g. thyroid storm); beta-blocker, supportive care and corticosteroids for severe thyroiditis; urgent endocrinology input.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; monitor glucose; begin insulin if needed; endocrinology input. Corticosteroids do not reverse beta-cell loss.
grades.2: Continue or withhold per glycaemic control; insulin; assess for ketoacidosis; endocrinology input. Corticosteroids do not reverse beta-cell loss.
grades.3: Withhold until glycaemia is controlled; insulin; assess and treat diabetic ketoacidosis; endocrinology input; resume once stable.
grades.4: Withhold and hospitalize; treat diabetic ketoacidosis with intravenous fluids and insulin; endocrinology input; resume once glycaemia is controlled. Corticosteroids do not reverse beta-cell loss.

grades.1: Any suspected myocarditis is high-acuity: withhold the checkpoint inhibitor and evaluate urgently; cardiology input; telemetry; high-dose systemic corticosteroids if myocarditis is confirmed.
grades.2: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; urgent cardiology input; high-dose systemic corticosteroids; telemetry; add second-line immunosuppression early if there is no rapid improvement.
grades.3: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize with telemetry; high-dose intravenous corticosteroids; urgent cardiology input; add second-line immunosuppression early.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize (ICU); high-intensity intravenous corticosteroids (pulse methylprednisolone for severe or unstable disease) and early second-line immunosuppression; urgent cardiology input and haemodynamic support.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; monitor renal function; rule out other causes (dehydration, obstruction, nephrotoxic drugs, contrast).
grades.2: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; exclude other causes; systemic corticosteroids; nephrology input; resume when improved toward baseline.
grades.3: Withhold or permanently discontinue per guideline; systemic corticosteroids; nephrology input; if no improvement within the guideline window, add second-line immunosuppression.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize; systemic corticosteroids and second-line immunosuppression for refractory disease; nephrology input and renal replacement therapy if needed.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; analgesia and NSAIDs; monitor symptoms.
grades.2: Continue or withhold per guideline; systemic corticosteroids if the response to NSAIDs is inadequate; rheumatology input.
grades.3: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; systemic corticosteroids; rheumatology input; consider DMARDs or biologics for refractory disease.
grades.4: Withhold or permanently discontinue per guideline; systemic corticosteroids and DMARDs or biologics for severe or refractory disease; rheumatology input.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor with close monitoring; exclude other causes. Watch for features of Guillain-Barre syndrome or myasthenia, which are neurologic emergencies.
grades.2: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; systemic corticosteroids; neurology input; exclude Guillain-Barre syndrome and myasthenia.
grades.3: Withhold or permanently discontinue per guideline; hospitalize; systemic corticosteroids; urgent neurology input; IVIG or plasmapheresis for Guillain-Barre-like or severe disease.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize (possible ICU) with respiratory monitoring; systemic corticosteroids and IVIG or plasmapheresis; urgent neurology input.

grades.1: Continue the checkpoint inhibitor; monitor haemoglobin and haemolysis markers; haematology input if needed.
grades.2: Withhold the checkpoint inhibitor; systemic corticosteroids; transfusion support as needed; haematology input.
grades.3: Withhold or permanently discontinue per guideline; systemic corticosteroids; transfusion support; haematology input; second-line immunosuppression for refractory disease.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; hospitalize; systemic corticosteroids, transfusion support and second-line immunosuppression for refractory disease; haematology input.

grades.1: Slow or interrupt the infusion; supportive care (antihistamine, antipyretic); monitor and resume at a slower rate once resolved. This is distinct from other irAEs and does not usually require immunosuppression.
grades.2: Interrupt the infusion; supportive care with antihistamine and antipyretic; consider corticosteroids; premedicate and slow the rate for future infusions.
grades.3: Interrupt or stop the infusion; treat with corticosteroids and supportive care; monitor closely; permanently discontinue for severe reactions per guideline.
grades.4: Permanently discontinue; treat anaphylaxis with epinephrine, corticosteroids, antihistamines and supportive care; hospitalize and monitor.
